mainTopic: טמנה and עירובי תבשילין in רבן גמליאל's house, setting up a candelabrum, extinguishing on יום טוב, and eye treatment on יום טוב and שבת
overview: The amud opens by finishing the question of why רבן גמליאל's household did not do טמנה on יום טוב for שבת. רב הונא says the case is someone with no עירובי תבשילין, and a ברייתא supports him. רבא gives a different explanation. אביי rejects it using חנניה's version of בית שמאי, and explains instead that the person made an עירוב for baking and cooking but not for insulating. Next, the גמרא explains that the ban on setting up a candelabrum applies to one made of segments, because בית שמאי hold that building applies to utensils. A long discussion of extinguishing on יום טוב follows: עולא's servant tilting a lamp, trimming a wick, putting out a lamp for marital privacy, and putting out a fire to save property. Each lenient challenge from the burning-log ברייתא is answered by saying it follows רבי יהודה. Then אמימר forbids eye medicine for a mild condition on יום טוב, but allows a גוי to apply it on שבת, because a helper's small role does not count (מסייע אין בו ממש). Finally, רב אשי challenges אמימר's permission to treat an eye on the second day of ראש השנה by quoting רבא on burial, and that challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the list of what is allowed without an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The end of רב הונא's list: even without עירובי תבשילין, one may light a lamp. In the name of רבי יצחק, one may also roast a small fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they may light a lamp for him. In the name of רבי יצחק they said: they may even roast a small fish for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list it started on the previous amud. The list says what a person who forgot to make עירובי תבשילין may still do on יום טוב for שבת. רבי יצחק adds one more item: a small fish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's point is that a person without an עירוב may still prepare the bare minimum for שבת: one loaf, one pot, and a lamp. This explains the משנה. Ordinary people may do a small amount of טמנה, but רבן גמליאל's house held like בית שמאי, who allow nothing without an עירוב. רבי יצחק stretches the minimum a bit to include a small fish.

keyTerms.meaning: Food set aside before יום טוב so that one may cook on יום טוב for שבת

phrases.english: and they may light the lamp for him.
phrases.notes: The last item in רב הונא's list, which began on the previous amud

phrases.english: In the name of Rabbi Yitzchak they said:
they may even roast a small fish for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This continues רב הונא's answer, which started on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without עירובי תבשילין, one may still make the minimum for שבת: one loaf, one pot, a lamp, and according to רבי יצחק a small fish.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the minimum-allowance rule
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same list, which supports רב הונא. It adds heating one small jug of water, and 'some say' a small fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught in a ברייתא: For someone who did not make עירובי תבשילין, they may bake one loaf for him, insulate one pot for him, light a lamp for him, and heat one small jug of water for him. Some say: they may even roast a small fish for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רב הונא. This shows his list is backed by an earlier source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא explicitly says 'טומנין לו קדרה אחת', meaning one may insulate one pot even without an עירוב. That is exactly the action the משנה is discussing. So the ברייתא confirms that ordinary people may insulate one pot without an עירוב, and רבן גמליאל's house was being strict. The 'יש אומרים' about the fish matches רבי יצחק's view.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא), bringing support
They insulate (wrap hot food to keep it warm)

phrases.english: It was also taught so (in a baraita):
One who did not set up an eiruv tavshilin —
they may bake one loaf for him,
and insulate one pot for him,
phrases.notes: This is the key line for the משנה's topic of insulating food

phrases.english: and light the lamp for him,
and heat one small jug for him,

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אַף צוֹלִין לוֹ דָּג קָטָן.
phrases.english: and some say: they may even roast a small fish for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the statement in step 1 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's rule that even without an עירוב one may make a minimal amount, including insulating one pot
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing one loaf, one insulated pot, a lamp, a jug of hot water, and (יש אומרים) a small fish
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's approach: the משנה is about someone with no עירוב. בית הלל allow a minimal amount, including one insulated pot. רבן גמליאל's house was strict like בית שמאי.

steps.title: רבא: an עירוב was made, but insulating is different
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the משנה differently. The person did make an עירוב. Still, insulating is a special case, because it clearly shows he is preparing for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really, it is a case where he did make the עירוב. Insulating is different, because it is obvious that he is doing it with שבת in mind.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to the earlier question of which case the משנה means. He says an עירוב was made, but טמנה is still a problem for בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooking on יום טוב can look as if it is for יום טוב itself, since some of the food could be eaten today. Insulating food late in the day is obviously only for tomorrow, שבת. According to רבא, בית שמאי forbid it even with an עירוב, because it so openly treats יום טוב as a preparation day for שבת.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Really, it is where he did set up (the eiruv) —
but insulating is different,
because the matter is evident
that he is doing it with Shabbat in mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation of the משנה's case than רב הונא's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: an עירוב was made, but טמנה is a special category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If an עירוב was made, even בית שמאי should allow insulating food.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with an עירוב, בית שמאי forbid טמנה because it is obviously for שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying טמנה is outside the normal rules of preparing on יום טוב for שבת. He is saying it is a special case within those rules, because its purpose is so obvious.

steps.title: אביי challenges רבא from חנניה's ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes חנניה's version of בית שמאי. One may insulate on יום טוב for שבת if he already had hot food insulated from ערב יום טוב. So בית שמאי do allow טמנה, even though it is obviously for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged him: חנניה says that בית שמאי say: One may not bake unless he made the עירוב with bread. One may not cook unless he made the עירוב with a cooked dish. One may not insulate unless he had hot food insulated from ערב יום טוב. So if he did have hot food insulated, he may insulate, even though it is obvious he is doing it for שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's answer. He uses a ברייתא showing that בית שמאי do allow insulating in the right circumstances.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said בית שמאי forbid טמנה because it is obviously for שבת. Yet חנניה reports that בית שמאי allow it whenever hot food was already insulated before יום טוב. That kind of עירוב for insulating makes it permitted. So 'it looks like it's for שבת' cannot be the reason בית שמאי forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who reports a specific version of בית שמאי's view

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
Chananya says: Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אוֹפִין אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עֵרֵב בְּפַת,
phrases.english: one may not bake unless he made the eiruv with bread,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מְבַשְּׁלִין אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עֵרֵב בְּתַבְשִׁיל,
phrases.english: and one may not cook unless he made the eiruv with a cooked dish,
and one may not insulate unless

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ לוֹ חַמִּין טְמוּנִין מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: he had hot food insulated from the eve of the Festival.
So if he had hot food insulated —
phrases.notes: The inference: the condition is met

phrases.english: in any case he may do it,
even though the matter is evident
that he is doing it with Shabbat in mind!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks רבא's reasoning in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that בית שמאי forbid טמנה because it is obviously for שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חנניה's ברייתא shows that בית שמאי allow טמנה when insulated food was set aside before יום טוב, even though it is still obviously for שבת. So obviousness is not the reason it is forbidden.

steps.title: אביי: an עירוב was made for one activity but not the other
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the משנה is about someone who made an עירוב for baking and cooking, but not one for insulating. The משנה follows חנניה's version of בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: It is a case where he made an עירוב for this but did not make one for that. And it follows חנניה, according to בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting רבא's answer, אביי gives his own explanation of the משנה's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to חנניה, בית שמאי require a separate עירוב for each kind of activity: bread for baking, a cooked dish for cooking, and insulated food for insulating. The person in the משנה made the עירוב for baking and cooking, but had no hot food insulated from before יום טוב. So he may not insulate. רבן גמליאל's house was strict and followed this view.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the previous answer and gives a new one)
For example / such as the case where
He made an עירוב for this, but not for that

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
Such as where he made an eiruv for this (baking and cooking)
but did not make an eiruv for this (insulating),
and it is (following) Chananya,
and according to Beit Shammai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's rejected answer with a new definition of the case, built on the ברייתא from step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case using a specific תנא's version of בית שמאי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא: an עירוב was made, but טמנה is forbidden because it is obviously for שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: An עירוב was made for baking and cooking but not for insulating. Following חנניה's version of בית שמאי, each activity needs its own עירוב.
steps.whatToRemember: Three answers to which case the משנה means. רב הונא: no עירוב at all. רבא: an עירוב was made, but טמנה is special (rejected by אביי). אביי: an עירוב was made for baking and cooking but not for insulating, following חנניה's version of בית שמאי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that according to חנניה, בית שמאי treat עירובי תבשילין as activity-specific. One type of עירוב does not cover a different type of preparation.

steps.title: What is wrong with setting up a candelabrum?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that one may not set up a candelabrum on יום טוב, and asks what forbidden act this involves.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One may not set up the candelabrum.' What forbidden thing is the person doing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next stringency of רבן גמליאל in the משנה: not standing up a fallen candelabrum on יום טוב. It asks what is actually forbidden about this, and so sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing a lamp upright seems like simply moving an object, and that is not one of the forbidden מלאכות. So the גמרא wants to know which מלאכה is involved. This question opens a new topic.

phrases.english: And one may not set up the candelabrum.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, one of רבן גמליאל's stringencies that follow בית שמאי.

phrases.english: What is he doing (that is forbidden)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the טמנה discussion to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which forbidden מלאכה is involved in setting up a candelabrum.

steps.title: A candelabrum made of pieces looks like building
steps.stepSummary: רב חיננא בר ביסנא explains that the case is a candelabrum made of separate segments. Putting it together looks like building. בית שמאי hold that building applies to utensils, and בית הלל hold that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חיננא בר ביסנא said: Here we are dealing with a candelabrum made of segments. Putting it together looks like building. בית שמאי hold that building applies to utensils. בית הלל hold that neither building nor taking apart applies to utensils.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The candelabrum is made of pieces that fit together, and reassembling it looks like building.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns the משנה into a disagreement between בית שמאי and בית הלל about whether 'building' applies to utensils. רבן גמליאל was strict like בית שמאי. According to בית הלל, one may put the pieces back together.
steps.whatToRemember: The ban on setting up the candelabrum applies only to one made of pieces. It follows בית שמאי's view that building applies to utensils. בית הלל disagree.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not about lifting a whole lamp that fell over. It is about putting separate pieces back together.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥinnana bar Bisna said:
Here we are dealing with a candelabrum made of segments,
which looks like building.

phrases.aramaic: דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי סָבְרִי: יֵשׁ בִּנְיָן בְּכֵלִים,
phrases.english: For Beit Shammai hold: there is building with utensils,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל סָבְרִי: אֵין בִּנְיָן בְּכֵלִים
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel hold: there is no building with utensils
and there is no dismantling with utensils.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The candelabrum is made of segments, and reassembling it looks like building. This is forbidden according to בית שמאי, who hold that building applies to utensils.

steps.title: עולא's servant tilts a lamp
steps.stepSummary: עולא visited רב יהודה's house, and עולא's servant tilted the lamp.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא came to רב יהודה's house. His servant got up and tilted the lamp.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. On יום טוב, עולא's servant tilted a burning lamp so that the oil would run away from the wick and the light would go out sooner. This story sets up רב יהודה's objection in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tilting the lamp does not put out the flame directly. It only makes the flame die out faster. The question is whether this indirect action counts as extinguishing.

phrases.english: Ulla happened to come to the house of Rav Yehuda,
his servant stood up and tilted the lamp.
phrases.notes: He tilted it so the oil would move away from the wick and the flame would go out sooner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Linked by the word זקף, which also appeared in the משנה. It opens a new discussion about extinguishing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A story in which a lamp was tilted on יום טוב, causing it to go out sooner.

steps.title: Taking oil from a lamp counts as extinguishing
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה challenges עולא from a ברייתא. Adding oil to a lamp is kindling, and taking oil out of it is extinguishing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה objected to עולא: One who puts oil into a lamp is liable for kindling. One who takes oil from it is liable for extinguishing!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה objects to what the servant did, using a ברייתא about שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking oil out of a burning lamp only makes it go out sooner, yet the ברייתא still counts it as extinguishing. Tilting the lamp does the same thing, so the servant extinguished on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: he raised an objection to him (from a source)
takes for himself, draws oil from

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda raised an objection to Ulla:
One who puts oil into the lamp —
is liable for kindling,
and one who takes oil from it —
is liable for extinguishing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the action described in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The servant's tilting of the lamp on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Making a lamp go out sooner by removing its oil counts as extinguishing. Tilting the lamp has the same effect, so it is forbidden.

steps.title: It was done without my knowledge
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that his servant acted without his knowledge.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It was not with my knowledge.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא does not defend the act. He says his servant did it on his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא agrees with רב יהודה that tilting the lamp counts as extinguishing. He only clears himself of blame. The הלכה stays as רב יהודה said.
steps.whatToRemember: Making a lamp go out sooner, even indirectly, counts as extinguishing.

phrases.english: He said to him: It was not with my knowledge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 9 by agreeing with it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concession: the act was the servant's, not עולא's.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that עולא approved of tilting the lamp.
steps.terutzMaskana: עולא agrees that it is forbidden. The servant acted on his own.

steps.title: Trimming a burnt wick is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that one may cut off the burnt end of a wick on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Trimming the burnt end of the wick is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a ruling: cutting off the charred tip of a wick on יום טוב is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After learning that making a light go out sooner is forbidden, we might think that touching the wick at all is forbidden. But trimming the burnt tip helps the lamp burn better, so it is not extinguishing.

keyTerms.meaning: the burnt (charred) end of a wick

phrases.english: Rav said: Trimming the burnt end of the wick is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of extinguishing on יום טוב with a lenient ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may trim the charred end of a wick on יום טוב.

steps.title: Putting out a lamp for marital privacy
steps.stepSummary: אבא בר מרתא asks אביי whether one may put out a lamp on יום טוב for marital relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא בר מרתא asked אביי: May one put out the lamp because of 'another matter'?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is asked about extinguishing on יום טוב: may one put out a lamp for the sake of marital relations? This sets up אביי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Marital relations are not allowed in a room with a lamp burning, so there is a real need here. The question is whether this need permits extinguishing on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: 'another matter', a polite way of saying marital relations

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'דבר אחר' does not mean 'something else' in general. It is a polite phrase for marital relations.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ אַבָּא בַּר מָרְתָא מֵאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Abba bar Marta asked Abaye:
What is the law about extinguishing the lamp
because of 'another matter'?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ אַבָּא בַּר מָרְתָא מֵאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another case about extinguishing on יום טוב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one may put out a lamp on יום טוב for marital privacy.

steps.title: Use another room instead
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that one may not put out the lamp, because it is possible to use a different room.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is possible in another room.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי says no. There is another way to have privacy, so extinguishing is not needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי first points to a simple alternative. Going to a different room solves the problem without putting out the lamp.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי's first answer points to another room. As the next steps show, he ends up forbidding putting out the lamp even when no alternative exists.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is possible in another room.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is forbidden, since one can use another room.

steps.title: What if there is no other room?
steps.stepSummary: אבא בר מרתא pushes further: what if the person has no second room to use?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he has no other room, what then?
steps.whatsHappening: אבא בר מרתא follows up on אביי's last answer by asking what to do if there is no other room.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי had said not to put out the lamp because the couple could go to another room. Now that option is taken away, so the question is whether putting out the lamp becomes allowed.

phrases.english: If he has no other room, what [is the law]?
phrases.notes: Still אבא בר מרתא asking אביי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Removes the option אביי relied on in Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether putting out the lamp is allowed when no other room exists.

steps.title: Make a partition
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the person can set up a divider instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is possible to make a partition for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives another way to avoid putting out the lamp: put up a divider in the room.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The divider blocks the light from the couple, just like another room would. So putting out the lamp is still not needed.

phrases.english: It is possible to make a partition for himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 14 with another option.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Set up a partition instead of putting out the lamp.

steps.title: What if he cannot make a partition?
steps.stepSummary: אבא בר מרתא asks what to do if no partition is possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he has nothing to make a partition with, what then?
steps.whatsHappening: אבא בר מרתא takes away the partition option as well and asks again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each answer is being tested by removing it. The question is whether, at some point, putting out the lamp becomes allowed.

phrases.english: If he has nothing with which to make a partition, what [is the law]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Removes the option given in Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether putting out the lamp is allowed when no partition is possible.

steps.title: Cover the lamp with a vessel
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that he can turn a vessel upside down over the lamp.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is possible to turn a vessel over it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a third option: cover the lamp with an upside-down container to hide its light.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Covering the lamp hides the light without putting out the flame. So no forbidden putting-out (כיבוי) takes place.

phrases.english: It is possible to turn the vessel over it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16 with yet another option.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Cover the lamp with a vessel.

steps.title: What if he has no vessel?
steps.stepSummary: אבא בר מרתא asks about the last case: no vessel either.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he has no vessel, what then?
steps.whatsHappening: אבא בר מרתא removes the final option, so now no alternative is left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the extreme case. The only remaining choice is to put out the lamp or not have relations.

phrases.english: If he has no vessel, what [is the law]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Removes the option given in Step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether putting out the lamp is allowed when no alternative remains.

steps.title: It is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that even then, putting out the lamp is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his final answer: even with no other option, one may not put out the lamp on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier options were not the reason for the ruling. Putting out a lamp for this purpose is simply not an allowed יום טוב need, so the lack of options does not change anything.
steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, putting out a lamp on יום טוב for marital relations is forbidden, even when nothing else is possible.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final answer to the series of questions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Putting out the lamp is forbidden.

steps.title: Challenge from the burning log ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: אבא בר מרתא quotes a ברייתא that allows putting out a log so the house or pot won't get smoky.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: One may not put out a log to save it from burning. But if he does it so the house or the pot won't get smoky, it is allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: אבא בר מרתא attacks אביי's ruling with a ברייתא that allows putting out a fire for a human need.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saving the wood itself is not allowed. But putting out the log to stop smoke is allowed, because it serves people's comfort. If that comfort need is enough, then putting out a lamp for marital relations should be allowed too.

keyTerms.meaning: he challenged him (from a תנאית source)
a piece of firewood, a log

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
One may not put out the log
in order to save it [from burning up],
but if it is so that it won't get smoky —
the house or the pot — it is permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling in Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's ruling that putting out a lamp is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows putting out a fire for a personal comfort need (no smoke), so putting out a lamp for marital relations should also be allowed.

steps.title: That ברייתא follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, but he himself rules like the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That ברייתא is רבי יהודה. When I spoke, I was following the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers by saying the ברייתא follows the opinion of one תנא, רבי יהודה, while his own ruling follows the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה allows a wider range of מלאכה on יום טוב for people's needs. The רבנן are stricter. So the ברייתא does not disprove אביי, who follows the רבנן.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָהִיא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא,
phrases.english: He said to him: That [ברייתא] is רבי יהודה,
when I spoke, [it was] according to the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a different תנא (מחלוקת תנאים).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is the accepted law, so it contradicts אביי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is רבי יהודה's view; אביי follows the stricter רבנן.

steps.title: Putting out a fire to save property
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רבה whether one may put out a fire on יום טוב only to prevent a money loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked רבה: May one put out a fire on יום טוב? If lives are in danger, I have no question, since that is allowed even on שבת. My question is about a case of only money loss — what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. אביי asks רבה about putting out a fire on יום טוב, and makes clear he only means a case of property loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Danger to life overrides even שבת, so that case is obvious. The real question is whether saving money is enough of a reason on יום טוב, where some מלאכה is allowed.

phrases.english: Abaye asked Rabba:

phrases.aramaic: מַהוּ לְכַבּוֹת אֶת הַדְּלֵקָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב?
phrases.english: What is [the law] about putting out a fire on a Festival?
Where there is danger to life —
I have no question,
since even on Shabbat it is permitted.
When I ask,
[it is] about loss of money — what [is the law]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, related question about putting out fires on יום טוב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether putting out a fire on יום טוב to prevent property loss is allowed.

steps.title: רבה rules it is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that putting out a fire only to save property is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה rules that one may not put out a fire on יום טוב just to save money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saving property is not one of the needs that allow מלאכה on יום טוב. So without danger to life, the fire may not be put out.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה, putting out a fire on יום טוב only to prevent a money loss is forbidden.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Putting out a fire for money loss is forbidden.

steps.title: The same log ברייתא challenges רבה
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה with the same ברייתא about putting out a log to avoid smoke.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: One may not put out a log to save it. But if he does it so the house or the pot won't get smoky, it is allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי quotes the same ברייתא again, this time against רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Smoke damage to a house or pot is a small loss, and the ברייתא still allows putting out the log to prevent it. So putting out a fire to prevent a bigger money loss should surely be allowed.
steps.confusionAlert: This is the exact same ברייתא as Step 20, but it is used for a different point. Before, it showed that comfort needs allow putting out a fire. Here, it shows that preventing a loss allows it.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
One may not put out the log
in order to save it,
but if it is so that it won't get smoky —
the house or the pot — it is permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבה's ruling in Step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that putting out a fire to save property is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If putting out a fire is allowed to prevent small smoke damage, it should surely be allowed to prevent a larger money loss.

steps.title: Same answer: it follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, while he rules like the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: That ברייתא is רבי יהודה. When I spoke, I was following the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives the same answer אביי gave earlier: the ברייתא is רבי יהודה's view, and his own ruling follows the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יהודה is more lenient about מלאכה on יום טוב, his ברייתא cannot disprove a ruling based on the stricter רבנן. Both rulings in this section stand.
steps.whatToRemember: Both אביי (putting out a lamp) and רבה (putting out a fire for money loss) rule strictly like the רבנן. The lenient log ברייתא is set aside as רבי יהודה's view.

phrases.english: That [ברייתא] is רבי יהודה,
when I spoke, [it was] according to the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 24 the same way Step 21 answered Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a different תנא (מחלוקת תנאים).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא allows putting out a fire to prevent loss, which contradicts רבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is רבי יהודה's view; רבה follows the stricter רבנן.

steps.title: רב אשי asks about putting medicine on the eye on a Festival
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks אמימר whether one may apply eye medicine on יום טוב. He clarifies that his question is only about non-dangerous eye conditions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked אמימר: May one paint the eye with medicine on יום טוב? Where there is danger, like the eye diseases רירא, דיצא, דמא, דמעתא, קדחתא, or the start of an eye inflammation, I have no question, because it is allowed even on שבת. My question is about the end of an inflammation, or medicine just to brighten the eyes. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks a new practical question: may you put medicine on your eyes on יום טוב? He narrows it down to cases where there is no danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dangerous eye conditions are already clear, because saving a life or a limb in danger overrides even שבת. The open question is about a mild condition. This connects to the earlier discussion of whether a forbidden act on יום טוב is allowed for a bodily need that is not food.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a formal question to a teacher or colleague)
To paint or smear the eye with ointment

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the question covers all eye problems. רב אשי openly says that dangerous eye problems are permitted even on שבת. He is asking only about mild cases.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi asked of Ameimar:

phrases.aramaic: מַהוּ לִכְחוֹל אֶת הָעַיִן בְּיוֹם טוֹב?
phrases.english: What is the law about painting the eye on a Festival?
Where there is danger, for example:
rira, ditza, dema, dimata, and kadachta (various eye diseases),
phrases.notes: Names of eye ailments: discharge, piercing pain, bleeding, tearing, and fever-heat in the eye.

phrases.english: and the beginning of an inflammation —
I have no question,
since even on Shabbat it is permitted.
Where I do have a question
is the end of an inflammation, or brightening the eyes. What is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question that parallels the earlier one (step 22) about doing a forbidden act on יום טוב for a non-food need.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether eye medicine for a non-dangerous condition (end of an inflammation, brightening the eyes) is allowed on יום טוב.

steps.title: אמימר rules it is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers that applying eye medicine for a non-dangerous condition on יום טוב is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר gives a short answer: it is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-dangerous medical treatment is not an eating need (אוכל נפש). So the permission of יום טוב does not cover it. This matches רבה's ruling about putting out a fire.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Painting the eye for a non-dangerous condition on יום טוב is forbidden.

steps.title: רב אשי challenges from the ברייתא about the log
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges אמימר from the ברייתא about the burning log. That ברייתא allows putting out a log to keep away smoke, which is a bodily comfort and not food.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: 'One may not put out a log' (but one may put it out so the house will not fill with smoke).
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks אמימר's ruling with the same ברייתא used earlier against רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allows putting out a fire to avoid smoke, which is a bodily need that is not food. Brightening the eyes is also a bodily need. So it should be allowed too.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him (from a תנאי source)
A piece of firewood, a log

phrases.english: He raised an objection: One may not extinguish a log,
phrases.notes: Shorthand for the full ברייתא quoted earlier, which goes on to permit putting it out to prevent smoke.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אמימר's ruling in step 27, the same way אביי challenged רבה in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's ruling that eye medicine on יום טוב is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא permits a forbidden act (putting out a fire) for a bodily comfort (avoiding smoke). So eye medicine for a bodily comfort should also be allowed.

steps.title: אמימר gives the same answer as before
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers as before: the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, but he rules like the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he answered him the way we answered earlier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not repeat the answer. It simply says אמימר answered the way רבה and אביי answered before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer was that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who widens what is permitted on יום טוב. אמימר follows the רבנן, who do not. So the ברייתא is not a problem for him.
steps.whatToRemember: On יום טוב, eye medicine for a mild problem is forbidden. The ברייתא that seems to allow comfort needs follows רבי יהודה, and the הלכה here follows the רבנן.

phrases.english: And he answered him as we answered.
phrases.notes: Points back to steps 21 and 25: the ברייתא is רבי יהודה, and we rule like the רבנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28 by reusing the earlier answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a different תנא (רבי יהודה), while the ruling follows the רבנן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be accepted halacha, permitting forbidden acts for bodily comfort.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is רבי יהודה's view. The רבנן, whom אמימר follows, forbid it.

steps.title: אמימר allowed eye medicine on שבת through a גוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that אמימר permitted having a גוי apply eye medicine on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר permitted painting the eye through a גוי on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a related practice: אמימר allowed a גוי to put medicine on a Jew's eyes on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is now different. It is not a Jew acting on יום טוב, but a גוי acting for him on שבת. Asking a גוי to do a forbidden act (אמירה לגוי) is more lenient when it is for someone who is sick.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not contradict step 27. There, a Jew himself applies the medicine on יום טוב, which is forbidden. Here, a גוי does the act, which is a much lighter matter.

phrases.english: Ameimar permitted painting the eye
by means of a gentile on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, related ruling of אמימר about eye medicine, now on שבת through a גוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew may have a גוי apply eye medicine to him on שבת.

steps.title: Another version: אמימר himself had it done
steps.stepSummary: Another version says אמימר himself had a גוי apply medicine to his eyes on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: אמימר himself had his eye painted by a גוי on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the story. In this version אמימר did not just rule. He actually did it himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה is the same in both versions. This version sets up the next challenge, because the person being treated takes part by opening and closing his eyes.

phrases.english: Some say:
Ameimar himself had his eye painted
by a gentile on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the report in step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אמימר personally had a גוי apply eye medicine to him on שבת.

steps.title: רב אשי asks what אמימר relies on
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks אמימר for his reasoning and suggests the sources he relies on: עולא and רב המנונא, who allow a גוי to do things for a sick person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: What is your reasoning? Is it what עולא son of רב עילאי said, that all the needs of a sick person may be done by a גוי on שבת? And רב המנונא said: anything that involves no danger, one tells a גוי and he does it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי identifies the basis for אמימר's leniency. He is setting up a challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sources allow asking a גוי to do forbidden work for a sick person who is not in danger. That explains why a גוי may apply eye medicine. Naming the source lets רב אשי show its limits.

keyTerms.meaning: The needs of a sick person
He tells the non-Jew, and the non-Jew does it

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule for practical הלכה: for a sick person who is not in danger (חולה שאין בו סכנה), one may ask a גוי to do forbidden work on שבת.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
What is your reasoning?
That which Ulla son of Rav Ilai said:
All the needs of a sick person
are done through a gentile on Shabbat,
and Rav Hamnuna said:
Any matter in which there is no danger —
one tells a gentile and he does it.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: קשיא (opening of the challenge in the next step)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind אמימר's practice in steps 30 and 31, as a setup for a challenge.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The basis for allowing a גוי to apply eye medicine on שבת. רב אשי suggests עולא and רב המנונא.

steps.title: But you help the non-Jew by blinking
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי argues that those sources apply only when the Jew does not help. אמימר did help, by closing and opening his eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: That applies only where the Jew does not help him. But you, Master, help him, since you close and open your eye!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי now makes his challenge. The leniency of using a גוי does not cover a case where the Jew takes part in the act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Closing and opening the eye spreads the medicine in. So the Jew is partly doing the act of healing himself. Once the Jew takes part, it is no longer purely the גוי's act.

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי, הֵיכָא דְּלָא מְסַיַּיע בַּהֲדֵיהּ.
phrases.english: These words apply where he does not assist him.
But the Master is assisting him,
since he closes and opens his eye!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי, הֵיכָא דְּלָא מְסַיַּיע בַּהֲדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the sources named in step 32 to challenge אמימר's practice.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's having eye medicine applied by a גוי on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The permission to use a גוי holds only when the Jew is passive. Blinking makes the Jew an active helper, so it should be forbidden.

steps.title: A mere helper's role is insignificant
steps.stepSummary: אמימר says רב זביד raised the same objection, and he answered him: a helper's contribution has no real substance (מסייע אין בו ממש).
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רב זביד holds like you, and I answered him: a helper has no substance.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר defends his practice. Small help to the one doing the act does not count as doing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גוי does the main act of applying the medicine. The Jew's blinking only adds a little to something that already works without it. The הלכה ignores this kind of help, so the leniency of using a גוי still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: A helper has no substance (his help does not count)

steps.whatToRemember: For a sick person not in danger, a גוי may do forbidden work on שבת. A Jew's small help along the way does not make it forbidden, because מסייע אין בו ממש.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule מסייע אין בו ממש is a basic principle of הלכות שבת. When one person does the act and another only adds minor help, the helper is not considered to have done the work.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִיכָּא רַב זְבִיד דְּקָאֵי כְּוָתָךְ,
phrases.english: He said to him: There is Rav Zevid, who holds like you,
and I answered him:
One who assists has no substance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge in step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Principle-based rejection: the act that is attacked is legally insignificant.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Blinking counts as the Jew taking part in the healing, which would cancel the leniency of using a גוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Help to an act that the main person can do alone has no legal weight, so the גוי alone is the doer.

steps.title: אמימר permits eye medicine on the second day of ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: אמימר permitted applying medicinal ointment to the eye on the second day of ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר permitted painting an eye with medicine on the second day of יום טוב of ראש השנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a new ruling: אמימר allowed someone to put healing ointment on an eye on the second day of ראש השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about having a גוי treat an eye on שבת. Here the case moves to the second day of יום טוב, which is less strict than the first day. אמימר treats the second day of ראש השנה as lenient enough to allow this treatment.

keyTerms.meaning: To paint or apply ointment to an eye (a medical treatment)
The second day of a festival
Rosh Hashanah, which has two festival days

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the base text for the challenge that follows. The question will be whether the second day of ראש השנה is as lenient as the second day of other festivals.

phrases.english: Ameimar permitted painting an eye (with medicine)

phrases.aramaic: בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה.
phrases.english: on the second day of the festival of Rosh Hashanah.
phrases.notes: The ruling is limited to the second day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the eye-treatment theme from אמימר's earlier rulings, but moves from שבת to the second day of ראש השנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Applying eye ointment is permitted on the second day of ראש השנה.

steps.title: רב אשי begins a challenge by quoting רבא on burial
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי quotes רבא: on the first day of יום טוב, a מת is buried by non-Jews; on the second day, Jews may bury him, even on ראש השנה. The quote continues into the next passage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: But didn't רבא say that if someone dies on the first day of יום טוב, non-Jews should handle his burial, and on the second day of יום טוב, Jews may handle it? And this is true even on the two days of ראש השנה...
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי starts to challenge אמימר by quoting a rule from רבא about burial on יום טוב. This step sets up the challenge, and its real point arrives when the quote finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's rule treats the second day of יום טוב leniently, so that even Jews may bury the dead. He specifies that ראש השנה is included for burial. That careful wording suggests that ראש השנה might be different in other matters, and רב אשי will use this against אמימר.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [he] say? (a formula that introduces a challenge from a known teaching)
They should attend to him (handle the burial)

steps.confusionAlert: So far, רבא's words sound lenient and seem to support אמימר. Don't stop here. The challenge comes from the end of רבא's statement on the next amud, which shows that ראש השנה's second day is not lenient in every way.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
But didn't Rava say:
If a person died on the first day of a festival,
non-Jews should attend to him (his burial);
on the second day of a festival,
Jews may attend to him.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ בִּשְׁנֵי יָמִים טוֹבִים שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה,
phrases.english: And this applies even on the two festival days of Rosh Hashanah,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְאַמֵּימָר, וְהָאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אמימר's ruling from step 35 by quoting רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's ruling that eye ointment is permitted on the second day of ראש השנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא spells out that ראש השנה is included in the burial leniency. That implies the second day of ראש השנה may be stricter in other matters, which would undercut אמימר's leniency. The full attack finishes on the next amud.
